bug_semantics: js_typed_array_sort with a user comparator sorts an index array, then rebuilds the typed array by reading array_tmp[array_idx[i]] without bounding j against the post-sort length. A comparator can shrink a resizable ArrayBuffer after large indices have already been moved to valid slots, so js_TA_cmp_generic's a_idx/b_idx >= count check never fires for those entries. After rqsort the function does len = min_int(len, p->u.array.count) and js_malloc(len * elt_size) for array_tmp, then copies with unbounded j, producing a heap-buffer-overflow read of the shrunken tmp (ASAN: 10-byte allocation from js_typed_array_sort when newSz=10 and leftover index 255).
flaw_origin: The overflow is not the 2020 snapshot reconstruction. It was first written in PR #646 member 878647e21dec1a101a5d7ced6134e70a8e2ffca8 (Ben Noordhuis, 2024-11-04), which added resizable ArrayBuffers and rewrote TA sort to (1) compare through live p->u.array.u.ptr with an incomplete OOB return-0 check, (2) shrink len after rqsort, and (3) reconstruct via p->u.array.u.uint*_ptr[i] = array_tmp[j] with no j < len test. Parent e569f39bf18b4670dd526b11ea09cd00d7be3e91 has no RABs, no maxByteLength/resize, and uses a fixed array_ptr snapshot plus a detach skip, so j cannot exceed the tmp allocation.
